problems: e63: pin ↔ axle-hole is not a compatible pair
notes: Page 2 builds the Naida mini-doll (hair, head, torso, legs) and puts a Trans-Dark Blue Tile Round 1x1 (b1) in her hand. The mini-doll pieces are not in the parts list or catalogue, so I did not record them. b1 therefore has no rests_on and no join edge.
The Goblin (lego-28849pr0041) is shown only as a finished figure, with no build step. I did not record it as placed on this page.
Step 1 places the first piece of the boat, a Reddish Brown Brick Wedged, Curved Inverted 6 x 4. It rests on nothing, so it has no edges.
Step 2 places two Medium Azure Plate 1 x 8 (b3, b4) side by side. Each clutches the brown hull piece b2, and they overhang the front of it.
I could not tell which studs each plate sits on, so the edges name no ports. The rests_on for b3 and b4 is [b2].
Step 3 adds the second Reddish Brown Brick Wedged, Curved Inverted 6 x 4 (b5). It is upside down on the opposite end of the two plates, so the hull now has a brown piece at each end.
Its anti-studs clutch the studs of b3 and b4, so rests_on is [b3, b4]. It does not touch b2, which is under the other end of the plates.
The edges name no ports because I could not tell which studs are used.
Step 4 adds two Reddish Brown Plate 1 x 2 (b6, b7), one at each end of the hull, on the studs of the hull bricks.

I took b6 to sit on b2 and b7 on b5, one per end. The picture does not show clearly which studs each plate uses, or whether either plate also touches the azure plates, so I recorded only the hull brick under each.
The edges name no ports.

Step 5 adds a Medium Azure Tile 2 x 2 with Groove (b8) and a Medium Azure Panel 1 x 2 x 1 (b9). Both sit across the two azure 1 x 8 plates, b3 and b4. The panel is next to the tile, nearer the middle of the boat.
The edges name no ports because I could not tell which studs each piece uses.
Step 6 adds two Dark Blue Plate Special 1 x 4 (b10, b11) along the two sides of the hull, and two Dark Blue Wedge Plate 4 x 4 with 2 x 2 Cutout (b12, b13), one at each end.
I guessed the supports: b10 and b11 rest on both hull bricks, b2 and b5. The wedge b12 rests on b2 and b13 on b5. The cutouts leave the brown plates b6 and b7 showing.
The edges name no ports.
Step 7 adds a Medium Azure Brick Curved 2 x 2 x 2/3 (b14), two Medium Azure Plate Special 1 x 1 with Vertical Tooth (b15, b16) and a Medium Azure Plate Special 1 x 2 Side Handle (b17).
I read b14 as sitting on the tile b8 and the stern wedge b13. The side handle b17 is on the stern wedge b13 at the tip of the boat.
I guessed the tooth plates: b15 on b11 and b16 on b10, one on each side plate. The picture does not show their position clearly.
The edges name no ports.
Step 8 adds two Dark Pink flowers (b18, b19) and a Pearl Gold jumper plate (b20).
The flowers go on the two tooth plates from the last step: b18 on b15 and b19 on b16. The jumper plate b20 is on the curved brick b14 at the stern.
The edges name no ports.
Step 9 builds a lantern: the Pearl Gold Plate Round 1 x 1 (b22) goes on top of the Trans-Medium Blue minifig head (b21), and the head sits on the jumper plate b20.
I identified the gold round piece as lego-6141 (Plate Round 1 x 1 with Solid Stud) from the parts list. It could also be the tile, but the stud is visible in the picture.
The lantern is the lantern in step 9, so b21 rests on b20 (stud.1.1) and b22 rests on b21.
Step 10 adds the curled gold prow ornament. The vine's bar (b24) goes into the bar holder (b23). The holder's clip then snaps onto the bar of the side handle plate b17 at the stern.
The red arrow shows the holder joining the vine. The black arrow shows the finished pair going onto b17. The order I used follows those two arrows.
I used clip/bar joins that can turn (revolute). The picture does not show how freely they move.
Step 11 adds the bow. A Pearl Gold wing-end wedge (b25) goes at the tip, and a Medium Azure Brick Curved 2 x 2 x 2/3 (b26) goes behind it.
Both pieces sit on the bow wedge plate b12. I also put b26 on the brown plate b6, which fills part of the cutout. The picture does not show clearly which studs each piece uses.
The edges name no ports.
Step 12 adds three pieces: a compass tile (b27), a map tile (b28) and a Dark Pink bag (b29).
I guessed the positions. The map tile b28 is on the two azure 1 x 8 plates, b3 and b4. The compass tile b27 is on the side plate b10. The bag b29 is on b3 near the front of the boat.
The bag has a clip, but I could not see what it grips, so I recorded a stud join only.
Step 13 puts two Trans-Bright Green gems (b30, b31) into the Dark Pink bag b29. They are loose pieces with no studs, so they get contact edges and rests_on is [].
The picture also shows the Naida mini-doll sitting in the boat. She is not in the parts list or catalogue, so I did not record her.
This page starts the second model, a rock hideout. Step 1 adds a Medium Azure Plate Round Corner 6 x 6 (b32) as the base. A Green Brick 1 x 4 (b33) sits along one straight edge of it.
b32 is the first piece of this model, so it rests on nothing.
The edge names no ports because I could not tell which studs the brick uses.
Step 2 adds a Green Brick 2 x 2 (b34) and a Light Bluish Gray Brick 2 x 2 (b35). Both sit on the azure base plate b32, next to the green 1 x 4 brick b33.
The picture does not show whether either brick also overlaps b33. I recorded only b32 as the support.
The edges name no ports.
Step 3 adds a Green Brick 2 x 2 (b36) and a Green Brick Curved 2 x 3 (b37) on top of the first layer. The curved brick sits at the right and forms the rounded side of the rock.
The exact supports are a guess. I put b36 on b33 and b35, and b37 on b33 and b34. The edges name no ports.
Step 4 adds a second Green Brick Curved 2 x 3 (b38) and a Light Bluish Gray Brick Sloped 75° 2 x 2 x 3 (b39).
I put b38 on top of b36 and b37. I put the slope b39 on the base plate b32, at the left front, beside the gray brick b35.
These supports are a guess because the picture is not clear on which studs are used. The edges name no ports.
Step 5 adds two Light Bluish Gray Brick Sloped 65° 2 x 1 x 2 (b40, b41) to build up the rock face.
I put b40 at the front on the base plate b32 and b41 on the gray 2 x 2 brick b35. This is a guess because the picture is not clear on which studs are used.
The edges name no ports.

Step 6 adds a Light Bluish Gray Tile Special 2 x 2 with Top Pin (b42) and a Lime Tile Round 2 x 2 with Green Foliage Print (b43). Both sit on the open studs of the azure base plate b32 in front of the rock.
The edges name no ports.
Step 7 adds a Lime jumper plate 2 x 2 (b44) on top of the rock and two Lime Plate Special 1 x 1 with Vertical Tooth (b45, b46) as moss or slime.
I put b44 on the slope b39 and the green brick b36. I put b45 on the slope b41 and b46 on the slope b40. These are guesses because the picture is not clear on which studs are used.
The edges name no ports.
Step 8 adds a Red flower (b47), a turkey drumstick (b48) and a small skeleton-bone piece (b49) on the rock.

I read the gray piece in the parts bin as lego-6266 Leg Skeleton. It could instead be the black Technic connector lego-92907, because the small icon is hard to read. I put it on the top studs of the curved brick b38.
I put the flower b47 on the lower tooth plate b46. I put the drumstick b48 on the centre stud of the jumper plate b44.
The edges for b47 and b49 name no ports.
Step 9 builds a small cannon. A Trans-Clear gem (b51) goes on the stud of a Dark Brown round support (b50). The pair then goes onto the gray piece b49 at the top of the rock, next to the drumstick.
The picture does not show how b50 attaches to b49, so I recorded a push-on join with no ports.
b50 lies on top of the rock and clutches nothing below, so I did not give it a rests_on.
Step 10 starts a new small sub-assembly with a Black Technic Axle and Pin Connector (b52). It has no connection yet.
Step 11 pushes a Red Technic Axle 2 Notched (b53) into one of the connector's axle holes. I chose axle-hole.1; the picture does not show which of the two holes is used.
The sub-assembly at the top of the page is the earlier model. I did not add it again.
Step 12 pushes the red axle b53 into the pin hole of a Dark Brown catapult (b54). The axle runs through the pin hole, so the catapult can swing on it.

Step 13 puts the Black Technic connector b52 onto the top pin of the gray tile b42 at the front of the rock. I used axle-hole.2 for this because b53 is already in axle-hole.1, but the picture does not show which hole is used.
The warning icon on the page is a caution not to look into the catapult when it fires. It adds no parts.

Step 14 builds a plant. The Lime cherries (b56) go onto the Magenta leaves (b57), and the brown carrot-top branch (b55) goes onto the same leaves. The finished plant then attaches at the front of the catapult mount.
I took the plant to attach to the Technic connector b52, near the catapult hinge. The picture does not show exactly which port or hole is used, so the edge names none on the b52 side.
The catalogue gives each of these plant parts a single bar port. I used bar.1 on the plant side where it applies, and the join methods are a guess.
Step 15 is built 2x. Each copy is a Dark Purple Plate Round 1 x 1 (b60, b61) on top of a Lime flower (b58, b59), like a plum or berry. Both copies then go onto studs of the catapult b54.
The picture shows only one copy placed and one beside it, so I assumed both end up on b54 studs. The edges name no ports.
Page 29 has no building step. It shows how the catapult works: the arm swings up and the plum pieces fly off, with a warning icon not to look into the catapult. It adds no parts or joins.
Page 30 has no building step. It shows both finished models, the gondola with Naida and the rock hideout with the goblin. It adds no parts or joins.
The goblin figure (lego-28849pr0041) and the Naida mini-doll are shown in place, but there is no step for either, so I did not record them.
Page 33 is advertising art for LEGO Elves, with the characters and the logo. It has no building step and adds nothing.
Page 34 is advertising art for LEGO Elves, with a small ad for sets 41181 and 41182. It has no building step and adds nothing.
Page 35 is advertising art for LEGO Elves, with small ads for sets 41184, 41183 and 41185. It has no building step and adds nothing.
Page 36 is an advertising page listing the other LEGO Elves sets and the goblin collection. It has no building step and adds nothing.
Page 37 is an advertisement for the free LEGO Elves app. It has no building step and adds nothing.
Page 38 is an advertisement for other LEGO themes (Disney Princess, Friends, DC Super Hero Girls and Elves). It has no building step and adds nothing.
Page 39 is an advertisement for the LEGO LIFE app. It has no building step and adds nothing.
Page 40 is the back cover. It is a product feedback and prize advert with trademark text. It has no building step and adds nothing.
Mini-doll and figure pieces (Naida mini-doll, goblin lego-28849pr0041) were not recorded, because no page showed a step that builds them or places them.
Several support and join choices in the rock hideout and boat steps were guesses from small pictures. They are flagged in the notes for those pages.

The stray piece was the Trans-Dark Blue bowl tile b1. It is held in Naida's hand. I now record the Naida mini-doll (b62), which was missing, as a new part type and join b1 to her hand. She sits in the boat, touching the tile b8 and the panel b9, so b1 is now part of the boat group.
The goblin (b63) was also missing. I recorded it standing on top of the rock on the green curved brick b38, as shown on page 30. The exact spot is a guess.

The booklet builds two separate models, the gondola (b2 to b31 with Naida and b1) and the rock hideout (b32 to b61 with the goblin). Nothing in the booklet joins them, so the two groups stay separate.
The two remaining groups are real. Set 41181 builds two separate models, Naida's gondola (b1 to b31, plus Naida b62) and the goblin's rock hideout with its catapult (b32 to b61, plus the goblin b63).
The booklet starts the rock hideout on page 16 with a new base plate (b32). It never joins that model to the boat, and the finished-model picture on page 30 shows them standing apart.
I added no edges, because any join between the two would be invented. All earlier pieces and edges stay as they were.
